meta: Aqua HK put HK$6,731 into Meta for 21 schedules, about HK$321 each — inside the good band and a clear recovery from 12 schedules the week before.
Dim Sum Library spent HK$1,378 for 6 schedules, roughly HK$230 each, its cheapest Meta week in the window but on a very small base.
Meta remains a thin last-click channel in Hong Kong: 27 combined schedules against 352 GA4 bookings across these two venues, so read the cost as awareness rather than acquisition.
google: Aqua HK Google ran HK$9,858 for about 77 booking conversions at roughly HK$128 CPA, inside the good band and up from 62 conversions the week before.
Dim Sum Library Google delivered about 66 conversions on HK$2,004 at roughly HK$30 CPA, comfortably the cheapest acquisition in the portfolio.
Both venues added spend and conversions week on week, so the Google side is not what is holding Dim Sum Library back.
ga4: Aqua HK users rose 15.7 percent week on week to 3,561 and bookings 18.9 percent to 208, converting at 5.8 percent against 4.9 percent last year; users are still 5.8 percent below last year, so the recovery is conversion-led.

Dim Sum Library users fell 10.2 percent week on week to 1,078 and are 4.2 percent below last year, with conversion at 13.4 percent against 17.7 percent last year — the single clearest gap in the Hong Kong portfolio.
Both venues sit behind on the FY-to-date line (Aqua HK −6.8 percent, Dim Sum Library −7.8 percent) while the other four are ahead.
